replacements.old: for (const d of ['/profile','/downloads','/temp','/home','/home/AppData/Roaming','/home/AppData/Local']) await ap(OUT + d);

rationale: Two concerns, one surgical patch. (1) HOME/USERPROFILE already redirect to OUT/home in LAUNCH.env, but Windows Chrome's file chooser resolves standard user folders (Desktop/Documents/Downloads) under USERPROFILE, so those subfolders are now pre-created inside the temporary HOME (plus AppData/Local/Temp) — keeping all dialog-side temp/user paths confined to OUT without touching the launch env. (2) The brand-new, experiment-owned profile at OUT/profile gets a minimal profile/Default/Preferences seeding only selectfile.last_directory to the absolute OUT/downloads, so the native chooser opens at the isolated downloads dir on first use. The write is merge-only (reads and preserves any pre-existing Preferences keys; the profile is newly created so nothing user-owned can be overwritten) and confined to the owned profile directory — no registry, global Chrome config, dependencies, or auth files are involved. All existing launch flags, chromiumSandbox/ignoreDefaultArgs isolation, offline mode, downloadsPath, cancel oracle, and ownership checks are left byte-for-byte unchanged. Note for the executor: this seeding is only an initial hint for the chooser's starting directory; if a scenario requires the dialog to start elsewhere, native navigation (typing/choosing a path in the dialog) remains allowed as a separate explicit step. This patch has not been exercised against a live browser — no test run is claimed; verification happens when the step11-visible-04 execution copy is launched.
